newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: LION SAYS AUSTRALIAN BEER PRICES TO RISE.
newsitem.headline: LION SAYS AUSTRALIAN BEER PRICES TO RISE.

text.p: The price of low-alcohol beer would rise by more than A$2.00 a case in some Australian states due to changes in taxation following a High Court ruling this week, New Zealand based brewer Lion Nathan Ltd said on Thursday.

Lion Nathan said it estimated that the industry faced an A$80 million increase in its annual tax bill because a 15 percent increase in federal government wholesale tax was greater than the aggregate of state taxes it has replaced.

The Australian government said on Wednesday it would replace about A$5 billion in annual petrol, alcohol and tobacco franchise fees levied by state governments with a new regime of uniform national taxes.
The revamp was forced by High Court decision on Tuesday that the franchise fees were unconstitutional as only the federal government could levy such fees.

Costello said he had agreed to the new plan, which was to take effect from midnight on Wednesday, only after the states assured him it would be set up and run in a way that did not raise tax revenues or prices.
Individual states, which have differing tax levels, would have to return excess funds collected to wholesalers to ensure prices and revenues did not rise.
However, the proposal attracted early criticism.
Cigarette manufacturer WD & HO Wills said on Wednesday it had been forced to suspend sales to assess the full implications of a "draconian" increase in tobacco excise.
Lion Nathan managing director Gordon Cairns said a system to return excess taxes to the industry did not exist and raised questions about the legality of such a system.

"We've received no substantive information from any government on how we should be operating after this change and what, if any, mechanism they propose to refund tax increases," Cairns said in a statement.
"Given the vacuum of information from government and conflicting statements by state governments we have no other option but to pass on, in full, tax increases to the retail trade," he said.
Low-alcohol beers would be most affectd in states which had taxed the product less than full strength beers, he said.
